questions.q: A SOC analyst sees hundreds of outbound DNS queries per minute to a single unfamiliar domain, each with a long random subdomain label. What activity does this most likely indicate?
choices: DNS tunneling for data exfiltration or C2
questions.why: High-volume queries with long random subdomains are the classic signature of DNS tunneling used to smuggle data or command-and-control traffic.

questions.q: While triaging an alert, an analyst wants to know which real-world adversary techniques map to observed behaviors so detections can be improved. Which framework is purpose-built for this?
questions.why: ATT&CK catalogs adversary tactics and techniques with observable behaviors; the others are governance or compliance frameworks, not TTP references.

questions.q: A vulnerability report lists a flaw with CVSS base score 9.8, but the affected service is on an isolated lab segment with no inbound access and no sensitive data. How should prioritization be adjusted?
choices: Patch immediately because base score alone dictates urgency
Escalate to legal for breach notification
Ignore it permanently since it is in a lab
Lower effective priority using environmental context despite the high base score
questions.why: CVSS base score is severity in the abstract; environmental factors like isolation and asset value refine true risk, so priority can be reduced.

questions.q: An analyst correlating logs notices a user account authenticated successfully from New York and, eight minutes later, from Singapore. What detection concept flags this?
questions.why: Two geographically distant logins within a window too short to travel indicates impossible travel, a strong account-compromise signal.

questions.q: During threat hunting, an analyst wants to test a specific hypothesis such as 'adversaries are using scheduled tasks for persistence.' What best describes this approach?
questions.why: Starting from a stated assumption about adversary behavior and searching data to prove or disprove it is hypothesis-driven hunting.

questions.q: A packet capture shows an internal host sending a small, fixed-size payload to an external IP at nearly exact 60-second intervals around the clock. What should the analyst suspect?
choices: C2 beaconing from a compromised host
questions.why: Regular, low-jitter, small-payload callbacks are the hallmark of malware beaconing to a command-and-control server.

questions.q: An analyst must choose a scan type that will find missing patches and misconfigurations on servers where valid admin accounts are available. Which scan gives the most accurate results?
questions.why: Credentialed scans log in to inspect installed patches and configs directly, producing far fewer false positives than unauthenticated scans.

questions.q: A SIEM rule fires whenever a single source IP triggers 50 failed logins within one minute across many accounts. Which attack does this rule best detect?
questions.why: Many failed authentications from one source in a short window indicates credential guessing such as brute force or spraying.

questions.q: After confirming a workstation is infected and actively spreading, the incident response team's immediate priority per the IR lifecycle is to do what?
choices: Contain the host to stop lateral movement
questions.why: In the containment phase the goal is to limit spread and damage before eradication and recovery; reporting comes later.

questions.q: An analyst reviewing a threat intel feed sees an indicator marked TLP:RED. How may this information be shared?
choices: With the entire company via email
Only with the specific recipients present, not onward
questions.why: TLP:RED restricts information to the named individuals in the exchange; it must not be shared further, even internally.

questions.q: Two separate scanners report a listening service as vulnerable, but manual testing shows the fix was already applied and the service is not exploitable. This scanner output is an example of what?
questions.why: A false positive is an alert on a condition that is not actually present or exploitable, as confirmed by manual validation.

questions.q: An analyst wants to enrich a suspicious file hash by checking many antivirus engines and community reports at once. Which resource is most appropriate?
questions.why: VirusTotal aggregates multi-engine detection and community intel for hashes, files, and URLs; the others are capture, scanning, and proxy tools.

questions.q: During log review, an analyst notices Windows Event ID 4720 events created just before large data transfers. What does 4720 represent, and why is it relevant?
choices: A service stopped, suggesting a crash
A successful logon, suggesting normal use
A user account was created, suggesting attacker persistence
An account lockout, suggesting a DoS
questions.why: Event ID 4720 is user account creation; a new account appearing before exfiltration can indicate an attacker establishing persistence.

questions.q: A remediation plan cannot patch a legacy medical device, but the flaw is remotely exploitable. Which compensating control most directly reduces exposure?
questions.why: When patching is impossible, segmentation limits who can reach the vulnerable device, directly reducing the attack surface.

questions.q: An analyst is building a detection and wants to reduce alerts on benign administrative PowerShell while still catching encoded, obfuscated commands. What is the best first step?
choices: Baseline normal admin activity, then alert on deviations like encoded commands
Block all scripting for all users
questions.why: Establishing a behavioral baseline lets the detection flag anomalous patterns such as EncodedCommand while suppressing routine admin noise.

questions.q: A CVSS vector includes AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N. What does this combination tell an analyst about exploitability?
choices: Only exploitable by an authenticated insider
Remotely exploitable with low complexity and no privileges or user interaction
Requires a victim to click a link
Requires local access and admin rights
questions.why: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges, and no user interaction describe an easily and remotely exploitable flaw, which raises urgency.

questions.q: An analyst receives a phishing report and wants to safely examine the embedded URL's true destination and content without risking the corporate network. What is the best approach?
choices: Open it in the analyst's browser
Forward it to all staff as a test
Click it from a domain admin workstation
Detonate it in an isolated sandbox
questions.why: A sandbox provides an isolated environment to observe URL and payload behavior without exposing production systems.

questions.q: SIEM correlation joins a failed IDS block, a successful login, and an unusual outbound connection from one host into a single incident. What is the primary value of this correlation?
choices: It reduces disk usage on the SIEM
It reveals an attack chain that individual events would miss
It eliminates the need for log retention
questions.why: Correlation stitches related low-level events into a higher-fidelity picture of an attack sequence that single alerts cannot show.

questions.q: An organization wants prioritized vulnerability remediation driven by which flaws are actually being exploited in the wild right now. Which resource best supports this?
questions.why: The CISA KEV catalog lists vulnerabilities with confirmed active exploitation, making it a strong signal for remediation prioritization.

questions.q: An analyst observes lsass.exe being accessed by an unusual process and credentials later reused across hosts. Which technique is most consistent with this?
choices: Credential dumping followed by lateral movement
questions.why: Reading LSASS memory is classic credential dumping; reusing harvested credentials on other hosts is lateral movement.

questions.q: A web server log shows requests containing ../../../../etc/passwd in the path. Which attack is being attempted?
questions.why: Sequences of ../ aimed at reaching files like /etc/passwd are directory traversal attempts to escape the web root.

questions.q: After eradication, the IR team restores systems from backups and monitors closely before declaring normal operations. Which IR phase is this?
questions.why: Recovery restores affected systems to production and validates they are clean and functioning before closing the incident.

questions.q: An analyst wants a structured way to describe a specific intrusion using adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim. Which model fits?
questions.why: The Diamond Model organizes an intrusion around adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim, ideal for analyzing single events.

questions.q: A scan flags a TLS service supporting only TLS 1.0 and RC4. What is the most accurate characterization for the report?
choices: A weak-cipher and deprecated-protocol finding to remediate
A false positive that can be ignored
questions.why: TLS 1.0 and RC4 are deprecated and cryptographically weak; this is a legitimate configuration weakness needing an upgrade to modern TLS.

questions.q: An analyst wants alerting to survive when attackers clear local logs. What control most directly preserves evidence?
choices: Forwarding logs to a centralized, write-protected SIEM in real time
questions.why: Shipping logs off-host to a central store as they are generated means local log clearing does not destroy the collected evidence.

questions.q: A threat intel report gives a confidence level of 'low' on attribution. How should the analyst treat this in decision-making?
choices: Immediately block based on attribution alone
Weight it cautiously and seek corroboration before acting
Discard all indicators in the report
questions.why: Low confidence means the assessment is uncertain; analysts should corroborate before taking high-impact action while still noting the IOCs.

questions.q: An analyst wants to detect data exfiltration hidden inside allowed HTTPS traffic to a cloud storage provider. Which data source is most useful?
choices: Network flow and volume metadata (NetFlow) plus DLP
questions.why: Flow metadata reveals abnormal outbound volumes even when payloads are encrypted, and DLP inspects content where decryption is available.

questions.q: A CVSS temporal score is lower than the base score for a given CVE. What most likely drove this reduction?
choices: No mature exploit exists and an official fix is available
questions.why: Temporal metrics reflect exploit maturity and remediation availability; an unproven exploit and an official patch lower the temporal score.

questions.q: An analyst identifies that a critical alert took hours to reach a human. To improve future response, which metric should be tracked and reduced?
questions.why: MTTD measures how long it takes to notice an incident; reducing it shortens attacker dwell time. ALE and RPO measure other things.

questions.q: A Linux host shows an unexpected cron entry that pulls and runs a script from a pastebin URL every 10 minutes. What is the primary concern?
questions.why: A cron job repeatedly downloading and executing remote code is a persistence mechanism that keeps re-running attacker payloads.

questions.q: During an incident, an analyst must collect evidence in a defensible way. Which practice most directly preserves admissibility?
choices: Working only on the live production disk
Maintaining chain of custody and hashing acquired images
Editing logs to remove noise before storage
questions.why: Documented chain of custody plus cryptographic hashing proves evidence integrity and who handled it, which supports legal admissibility.

questions.q: An analyst tuning a noisy IDS signature finds it alerts on legitimate vulnerability-scanner traffic every night. What is the best tuning action?
choices: Add an exception for the known scanner source and schedule
Ignore all IDS alerts going forward
questions.why: Whitelisting the authorized scanner's source and window removes known-benign noise while keeping the detection active for real threats.

questions.q: A report shows that a public-facing app has a SQL injection flaw. Which remediation addresses the root cause most effectively?
questions.why: Parameterized queries separate code from data so user input cannot alter query structure, eliminating the injection root cause.

questions.q: An analyst wants a repeatable, machine-readable way to exchange threat intelligence with a partner organization. Which pair of standards is designed for this?
questions.why: STIX structures threat data and TAXII transports it, enabling automated intel sharing. The other pairs handle monitoring, SSO, and AAA.

questions.q: Endpoint telemetry shows rundll32.exe launched with a suspicious command line spawning cmd.exe and then powershell.exe. What analysis technique best explains this relationship?
questions.why: Examining parent-child process chains reveals suspicious spawning patterns that indicate living-off-the-land execution.

questions.q: A vulnerability affects only a specific software version. Before mass remediation, what should the analyst do first to scope the work?
choices: Reboot every server in the environment
Notify all customers of a breach
Query the asset inventory to identify affected hosts
questions.why: Accurate scoping starts with an asset and software inventory to find which hosts actually run the vulnerable version.

questions.q: An analyst notices an alert volume so high that real incidents are missed. Which concept describes this operational problem?
choices: Alert fatigue driven by low signal-to-noise
questions.why: Excessive, mostly-benign alerts desensitize analysts and cause true positives to be overlooked, known as alert fatigue.

questions.q: A phishing email passed SPF but the display name spoofs the CEO and the reply-to is an external gmail address. What check best exposes this?
choices: Inspect email headers for reply-to and return-path mismatch
questions.why: Header analysis of reply-to and return-path reveals spoofing that a passing SPF on the sending domain does not prevent.

questions.q: An analyst must recommend how often internal vulnerability scans run for a PCI-relevant network. What factor should most drive the cadence?
choices: The color scheme of the dashboard
The number of analysts on shift
questions.why: Scan frequency is driven by compliance mandates and how critical the assets are, balancing risk against operational load.

questions.q: During hunting, an analyst finds a beacon but wants to know what other hosts talked to the same C2 IP over the past 30 days. Which SIEM capability supports this?
choices: Historical log search across retained data
questions.why: Searching retained historical logs lets the analyst pivot on the C2 indicator to find every host that contacted it over time.

questions.q: A zero-day is being exploited and no patch exists. Which action provides the fastest risk reduction while a fix is developed?
choices: Wait for the vendor patch with no other action
Deploy a virtual patch / WAF or IPS signature to block the exploit
questions.why: A virtual patch at the WAF or IPS blocks the specific exploit pattern, buying time until a real code fix ships.

questions.q: An analyst writes a detection rule and wants to measure its quality before production. Which pair of outcomes should be minimized?
questions.why: A good detection minimizes both false alarms and missed detections; balancing these determines the rule's real-world value.

questions.q: A SOC receives an IOC list of malicious IPs from an ISAC. What is the most effective immediate use of this feed?
choices: Print it and file it in a binder
Ingest it into the SIEM and firewall for automated matching and blocking
questions.why: Operationalizing shared IOCs by feeding them into detection and blocking tools turns intel into automated protection.

questions.q: An analyst observes a service account interactively logging into workstations at 3 a.m., which it never does. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Anomalous behavior possibly indicating account compromise
questions.why: Service accounts should not log in interactively; off-hours interactive use is a behavioral anomaly suggesting compromise or misuse.

questions.q: When communicating a critical finding to non-technical executives, which reporting approach is most effective?
choices: Frame it in business risk and impact terms with a clear recommendation
Send only the SIEM query syntax
List every CVE number without context
questions.why: Executives need risk, impact, and a recommended action, not raw technical artifacts, to make timely decisions.

questions.q: An analyst wants to prioritize which of 5,000 findings to fix first when CVSS scores are similar. Which added factor best sharpens prioritization?
choices: The age of the operating system logo
Exploitability and asset exposure to the internet
questions.why: Among equal severities, internet-facing exposure and known exploitability determine which flaws are most likely to be attacked first.

questions.q: A memory-resident threat leaves little on disk but shows up as anomalous behavior in running processes. Which technique best detects it?
choices: Comparing file hashes against a static allowlist only
Behavioral / heuristic analysis of live process activity
questions.why: Fileless malware evades signature and hash checks, so behavioral analysis of in-memory process activity is needed to catch it.

questions.q: After an incident closes, the team holds a review to capture what worked and what to improve. What is the main output of this lessons-learned phase?
choices: Actionable improvements to controls and the IR playbook
questions.why: The post-incident review feeds concrete improvements back into detections, controls, and playbooks to strengthen future response.

questions.q: An analyst needs to confirm whether a suspicious binary makes network connections and modifies the registry when run. Which analysis method provides this?
choices: Dynamic (behavioral) malware analysis in a sandbox
questions.why: Dynamic analysis executes the sample in an instrumented sandbox to observe runtime behaviors like network and registry activity.

questions.q: An analyst correlating logs from three systems finds the event timestamps are minutes apart for the same action, making the timeline unreliable. What is the root fix?
choices: Switch the SIEM to a different vendor
Synchronize all sources to a common NTP time source
questions.why: Accurate correlation requires consistent clocks; syncing every log source to NTP aligns timestamps so an incident timeline is trustworthy.
